idea-pd26-1883-code-of-indian-offenses.title: When US law banned ceremony: the 1883 Code of Indian Offenses

summary: In 1883 the Interior Department wrote rules that made the sun dance and the work of medicine men Indian offenses, punished by lost rations or jail.
No act of Congress created the Court of Indian Offenses. A federal judge upheld it in 1888, and the 1904 rules named so-called religious ceremonies.
Congress declared a policy of protecting Native religions in 1978. The court still sits today as five CFR courts, and its code has no religious offenses.
start_here.how_sure_note: The rules, annual reports, court opinions, statutes and the current code were read from the government's own pages. The counts of cases come from one law review study that relies on what agents chose to report, and this research did not find when the dance rules left the regulations.

summary: Courts, regulators and lawmakers in the United States, Australia and Mexico keep asking brands three questions about Indigenous designs: where is it from, who said yes, and what goes back.
The Navajo Nation's case against Urban Outfitters, U.S. prosecutions under the Indian Arts and Crafts Act and Australia's Birubi Art penalty turn on false claims about where goods came from.
Mexico's 2022 law writes consent, credit and shared benefits into its articles, but it faces a constitutional challenge that is still open.
start_here.how_sure_note: The court papers, statutes and official releases were read, and an independent check on November 23, 2026 compared every quotation with its source. This is sure about what those pages say; it cannot say what the confidential Navajo settlement returned, or how Mexico's Supreme Court will rule on the 2022 law.

summary: In 2008 the Inter-American Court told Suriname that the Saramaka decide who speaks for them, and the 2007 UN declaration says the same.
When outsiders skipped that step, as in the Havasupai blood study and a genome study of four San men, communities objected and sued or wrote new rules.
Some peoples have built a front door: the San Code of 2017, a healers' protocol and a rooibos levy paid to the Khoi and San.

summary: A 2024 Boston University thesis takes its title from a father's warning: "You have two strikes against you: You are a woman. And you are Black."
Black women wrote down the same double burden long before, from Anna Julia Cooper in 1892 to Shirley Chisholm and Frances Beal in 1969.
The study could match only 49 Black adults from Framingham Heart Study data, and it reported plainly that its hypothesis was not supported.
start_here.how_sure_note: Every quotation was compared word for word with its source on November 23, 2026. This is sure about what the pages say; the study itself settled nothing, and the thesis calls its results preliminary.

summary: In May 2024 OpenAI paused its ChatGPT voice Sky after Scarlett Johansson said it sounded like her; OpenAI said the voice belonged to a different actor cast before any outreach to her.

Tennessee's 2024 law, California's 2024 labor code rule and the federal NO FAKES bill each reach voice replicas in different ways.

ioo-c01-p07.title: Paid work is not automatically work made for hire

summary: Under the Copyright Act, work made for hire has only two routes: an employee's work within the job, or a commissioned work in one of nine categories with a signed writing.
In Community for Creative Non-Violence v. Reid (1989), a unanimous Supreme Court held that a sculptor paid $15,000 was an independent contractor, so his statue was not a work made for hire.
NASA credits Richard Danne and Bruce Blackburn with its 1975 worm logo, but its public papers do not show who owned the rights; only the contract could.
start_here.how_sure_note: Built from the Supreme Court and appeals court opinions, the Copyright Act, Copyright Office guidance and NASA's own papers, read in full. What happened in the Reid case after 1989 is not in any free published opinion, and the NASA contract is not public. An independent check corrected 17 of 66 claims and left none wrong. Education, not legal advice.

ioo-c01-p09.title: Embed, host or repost? Big Buck Bunny on YouTube

summary: Big Buck Bunny is a free film the Blender Foundation released in 2008 under Creative Commons BY 3.0, and its makers put it on YouTube themselves.
Hosting a file, embedding a host's player and reposting a new copy are three different acts with three different paper trails.

summary: In Hawaiʻi the public shore runs up to the highest reach of the winter waves, shown by plants or a line of debris.

summary: A 1958 Dutch decree exempted hemp grown for seed, fiber or only as a windbreak from part of the drug ban; in 1971 a defendant read it to an Amsterdam court under a name he made up.
The 1976 Opium Act made 30 grams or less of hemp or hashish a minor offense, legalized nothing, and redefined hemp as every part of the plant except the seeds.

Tolerance came from prosecutors' guidelines of October 1976; the windbreak exemption was dropped in 1999, and since April 7, 2025 coffee shops in ten municipalities sell only hemp from state-named growers.

Educational information, not legal advice.

summary: A federal hemp sentence excludes viable seeds from a plant over 0.3 percent total THC, counting THCA. It is set to start December 11, 2026, unless Congress acts again.
Hawaii already bars selling viable hemp seeds except to licensed hemp producers or permitted processors, and its penal code counts seeds as marijuana.
Hawaii's medical law names three sources of cannabis for patients but no lawful source of seeds. Education, not legal advice.

summary: Hawaii section 521-39 voids a lease clause allowing eviction of a tenant with a valid medical cannabis certificate, unless the lease allows eviction for tobacco smoking and the cannabis is smoked.

Condominium and planned community sections void certain discriminatory provisions, but section 521-39 does not apply where association documents prohibit medical use, and none of the sections mentions growing.
Federally assisted housing follows federal rules, and a cultivation license rule is set to take effect January 1, 2028, with no text found on how it applies to patients.
start_here.how_sure_note: Every legal statement quotes or paraphrases the statute or federal text it cites, read on the legislature's data site and checked again by an independent check on November 12, 2026. No landlord may refuse to lease to a person solely for status as a patient or caregiver, unless the landlord would lose a federal benefit.

summary: Hawaiʻi's health department points residents to the National Cannabis Study for people about to start, Realm of Caring's registry for current users, and COSMIC, an observational cancer study with 13 listed Hawaiʻi sites.

The state's 2022 patient survey was opt-in, and a 2024 study found Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander participation undocumented for 6 of 10 drug products' trials, so who joins shapes what research can say about Hawaiʻi.
All three studies are observational: they can show patterns, not cause. No public source gives Hawaiʻi enrollment, and federal consent rules give the questions to ask before joining.
start_here.how_sure_note: Each study detail comes from the study's own pages, its federal grant or trial listing, or the state's pages, and every source was fetched again and checked against the text by an independent fact checker on November 11, 2026. Several things are not public: Hawaiʻi enrollment, the registry's consent form, and whether NCS blood results go back to participants. Education, not medical advice.

summary: Hawaiʻi's OMCCR says a dispensary may not be subject to HIPAA, but a Department of Health rule requires it to keep a patient's identity and medical condition confidential.
A provider, the registry, the dispensary and a statewide tracking system each hold part of a patient's information, under different rules.
Police can verify registration at any hour, and the registry check has mattered most for gun permits.
start_here.how_sure_note: The statutes, rules and federal texts were read directly, and this post was independently fact checked on Nov 24, 2026. Some questions, such as whether any dispensary is a HIPAA covered entity, are not answered by any public source found.

summary: Hawaiʻi tests dispensary cannabis against a list of 56 pesticide entries, each with a limit of 1.0 ppm, and a batch over any limit cannot be sold.
Food runs on a different rulebook: EPA sets a tolerance for each pesticide, food by food, and in 2017 it said none existed for marijuana or hemp.
Pesticides are not on the list of failures a Hawaiʻi dispensary may remediate, and how the state chose 1.0 ppm is not explained in any document found.

Lab failure rates come only from a private lab in news reports, and no state data on pesticide failures was found.

Since February 24, 2022, the rule lists organisms that must not be detected in one gram; today there are six: E. coli, Salmonella and four Aspergillus molds.
OMCCR's page names one certified lab, on Oʻahu, and the rules stay interim until July 1, 2027 or until standard rules are adopted.

rnc-mjbp2702-virginia-2027-date-by-date.title: 2027, date by date: how Virginia's cannabis market opens

summary: Virginia's 2026 budget act, House Bill 30, Chapter 1, writes the 2027 calendar for the state's retail cannabis market into Item 4-14.
The market dates are February 1, March 1, May 1, June 1, July 1 and November 1, 2027; no licensee may sell at retail before July 1, 2027, medical dispensing aside.
Many dates are "may" dates, the earliest a step can happen, and the Authority's own rules were not checked for this piece.
start_here.how_sure_note: Every date and duty is quoted from the enacted text of Item 4-14, read in full from enactment 8 to 38 and checked again by an independent check on November 11, 2026. The Authority's rules were not checked, and "may" dates are not promises. Education, not legal advice.

Its survey matched BioTrack sales for March at 98.6%. Its tourism and year-five figures are survey answers and model projections.
Adult-use bills did not move in 2026, and since April 28, 2026 marijuana under a state medical license is federal Schedule III. Education, not legal advice.

Act 241 of 2015 created eight dispensary licenses. Registered patients peaked at 35,444 in August 2021 and fell to 30,035 by November 2024.
Adult-use bills lacked the votes in 2026. Since April 28, 2026, marijuana under a state medical license is federal Schedule III. Education, not legal advice.

A 2016 University of Vermont study scored 1,327 books and found six shapes; the most downloaded were not the happy rise.

rnc-sweep-content-strategy-system-21.title: Two thirds of Google searches now end without a click

summary: From January to April 2026, about 68 percent of US Google searches in Similarweb's browsing panel ended without a click, and 232 clicks per 1,000 searches reached the open web.
Click studies by Ahrefs, Seer Interactive and Pew all found fewer clicks when an AI summary appears, and news sites measured a 33 percent fall in Google search referrals in a year.
Google says total clicks are relatively stable but has published no totals, so no outside reader can test that claim.
start_here.how_sure_note: The 68 percent figure is solid as far as the panel can see, but it misses searches in the Google app. The ten-year trend joins three different panels, so read it as direction. The click studies are vendor studies that measure narrow things. Google's claim cannot be checked without its numbers.

summary: The RN Collins studio calendar planned eight photo carousels from a trip to the Netherlands in October 2026.
Dutch law limits publishing portraits, and the Dutch privacy authority says a recognisable person in a photo is personal data, so a public brand post falls outside the household exception.
Each venue has its own rules: the Philips Museum bars commercial use of inside photos without written permission, and the Rijksmuseum bars photos in its exhibition wing and Cuypers Library.

tfh-hi-c14-03.title: After Hilo Had No Warning, Hawaiʻi Helped Build a Pacific One

summary: On April 1, 1946, a tsunami from the Aleutian Islands reached Hilo almost five hours after it formed, with no warning.
In 1948, the United States set up its first tsunami warning operation at the Honolulu observatory.
The system's later tests in 1952, 1957 and 1960 showed that a warning works only when people act on it.

tfh-hi-c14-04.title: When Two Versions of the Law Disagree

summary: The Hawaiian Kingdom published its laws in Hawaiian and English, drafted in one and translated into the other.
In 1856 its Supreme Court said the Hawaiian governs when the texts irreconcilably differ. The 1859 Civil Code and an 1865 act made English binding instead.
HRS section 1-13 still makes the English binding. Bills in 2023, 2025 and 2026 to change that did not become law.

summary: In 1913 a sugar company drove a tunnel under Oʻahu's Koʻolau Range to carry windward stream water to its leeward cane, and struck far more water than anyone had measured.
The system runs 26.5 miles from Kahana Valley to Kunia, with 2.76 miles of main tunnel under the crest, and has carried water since 1916.

tfh-hi-c14-08.title: The Gate That Thinks With the Tide

summary: Heʻeia Fishpond in Kāneʻohe Bay is enclosed by a stone wall about 1.3 miles long, with seven gates, mākāhā, that admit water and young fish and keep grown fish inside.
A 1965 flood broke the wall, and mangrove and lost stream flow damaged the system; Paepae o Heʻeia, founded in 2001, has rebuilt it, and the last gap was filled in December 2025.
Measurements after the repair showed water now moves through the gates and leaves the pond sooner, but the pond still gets too little fresh water.

summary: The Air Force opened a tracking station on the ridge above Kaʻena Point in 1959, and its first job was secret: helping bring CORONA film home from orbit.
After a long run of failures, the first fully successful CORONA mission came in August 1960, when an aircraft caught a film capsule in midair.
CORONA ended in 1972, its imagery was declassified in 1995, and the station was renamed Kaʻena Point Space Force Station in 2021.

tfh-hi-c14-11.title: The Lines That Changed the Land

summary: From 1846, Hawaiʻi's Land Commission asked claimants to turn the land they lived on into written claims, testimony, surveys and awards.
The 1848 Māhele divided interests among the king and chiefs by land name, and the 1850 act gave native tenants title to house lots and cultivated land, which came to less than 1 percent of the land.
Surveys were uneven, many large lands were awarded by name, and courts still read these 19th-century papers in land disputes.

tfh-hi-c14-13.title: Hawaiʻi Once Powered a Barge with the Temperature Difference in the Ocean

summary: On August 2, 1979, the Mini-OTEC barge off Keāhole Point made more electricity than it used.
It ran on the temperature gap between warm surface water and cold water from about 2,000 feet down, and kept about 10 of about 50 kilowatts.
It showed the cycle could work at sea. It did not show that ocean thermal power could pay its way.

tfh-mj-s01-medical-cannabis-in-the-nevad.title: Nevada put medical cannabis in its constitution

summary: Nevada voters approved Question 9 in 1998 and again in 2000, and it became Article 4, section 38 of the state constitution.
The section orders the Legislature to provide by law for patient use, rules for minors, forfeiture protection, a confidential registry and methods of supply.
It sets limits too, and the Legislature answered it in 2001 with AB 453. Education, not legal or medical advice.

The rules cover batch numbers, tags, manifests, quarterly counts and the named reasons allowed for each fix.
As of November 8, 2026, the detailed hold-order rules and a tagging change were adopted or proposed but not in force.

tfh-mj-s07-a-regulator-from-the-casino-f.title: Nevada borrowed its cannabis regulator from the casino floor

summary: In 2019 Nevada created a Cannabis Compliance Board that its bill calls "generally modeled after the Nevada Gaming Control Board."
The law borrowed gaming's purpose language, board seats, character test and exemption from the state's rulemaking act, and it used one board where gaming has two tiers.
In 2023 and 2025 lawmakers ended the exemption and moved discipline hearings to hearing officers.

tfh-mj-s09-ten-lounge-licenses-for-socia.title: Nevada reserved ten lounge licenses for social equity. Then the process kept going.

The Board drew 10 of 30 applicants in 2022. A 2024 audit found six were not eligible, and a second draw filled their places.
As of October 2026, three social equity applicants hold conditional licenses and none of their lounges is open. Education, not legal advice.

tfh-nl-venue-sectie-c.title: Sectie-C, 2015 to 2024: a former factory site in the Dutch Design Week archive

summary: Sectie-C is a block of factory halls in Eindhoven's Tongelre district where electrical equipment was made until 2007; from 2010 artists and designers moved in.
It became a Dutch Design Week location from 2011, and the DDW photo archive holds Sectie-C albums from 2015 to 2024, with none found for 2023 or 2025.
The city council adopted a plan for the site in 2024, and in 2026 the city's preferred scenario was to buy the creative workspace; no source found shows the purchase completed.
start_here.how_sure_note: Built from public registers, newspapers, council papers, the developer's and tenants' pages and the DDW photo archive, read on October 13, 2026. Three things stay open: who owned the factory when it closed, whether any hall was built for Philips before 1970, and how big the site is.

could_be_wrong.point: Who owned the factory when it closed in 2007 is not settled: one local history column says Strukton, and no other source found names a later owner.
A Philips origin for part of the complex rests on one local history column; the building register dates no hall before 1970.
The site is given as 6, almost 8 or 11.3 hectares, and no source says what is in or out.
The March 3, 2026 council letter could not be opened; the purchase paragraph rests on the city's handover document and two trade reports.
Flickr shows only part of the album list to a visitor who is not signed in, so missing years rest on a search of the account.
